::: {#rem-information-gain}
#### Information gain in decision trees

A decision tree splits the points at a node into branches
and scores the split by its **information gain**:
the entropy of the class labels at the node,
minus the entropy left in the branches,
each branch weighted by its share of the points [@quinlan1986induction].
Draw one point uniformly at random from the node,
and let $Y$ be its class and $X$ the branch it falls into.
Then the entropy at the node is $H(Y)$,
the weighted entropy left in the branches is $H(Y \mid X)$,
and the information gain is the [mutual information](#def-mutual-information) $I(X; Y)$.

:::
